title: Dynamite Lumpia (Serrano and Pork)
summary: Seeded serrano chiles stuffed with garlicky pork filling, rolled in lumpia wrappers with the stems poking out, and fried until crisp; mildly spicy.
notes: Video: 'Crispy Spring Rolls At Home (Lumpia)' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/post/easy-filipino-lumpia-recipe (serves 6, prep 30 min, cook 30 min for the page as a whole; 35-40 wrappers for the original lumpia). The video holds three versions (original pork, dynamite with serrano, cheese); each has its own file, all pointing to this transcript, and the shared sauce, filling and frying lines are repeated. This file is the dynamite version. Serranos: the video says about five to six if making only this version, the page says 10; the video wins, midpoint 5 1/2 at about 6 g each (our estimate). One serrano (two halves) fills one wrapper, which is cut into two pieces, so 5 1/2 serranos make about 11 pieces. That cannot use the whole ~1,348 g filling batch, so the filling and wrappers are scaled to what the peppers use (our estimate): about 30 g of filling per piece (the original uses about 35 g per roll), 11 x 30 = about 330 g, entered as 1/4 of every stated filling amount (about 337 g); 5 1/2 wrappers; egg wash scaled from the page's 1 egg for 10 serranos. Servings: about 11 pieces, at roughly 6 pieces a serving like the original (38 rolls for 6), gives 2 servings (estimated). Times are the page's figures for the whole recipe, applied here (estimated). The sweet chili sauce (all amounts stated) is a dipping sauce served on the side, as are the Kewpie mayo and banana ketchup, so none of them is counted. Frying oil (2 1/2-3 quarts in the video, 2 quarts on the page) is excluded; absorbed oil is counted at 10% of the raw weight of the rolls (house rule). Our estimates also: 15 g per wrapper, celery rib 40 g. Serrano uses the existing fresh green chili slug, weighed in grams. The sauce lines show the full sauce batch (excluded anyway). Lumpia wrappers use USDA wonton/egg roll wrappers (proxy), at our estimate of 15 g per wrapper. Banana ketchup uses tomato ketchup as its proxy (excluded anyway).

steps.text: Sweet chili sauce: trim, seed and finely chop the Fresno chiles; finely mince the garlic and set it aside.
In a small pot, stir the chiles with the sugar, water and vinegar. Boil over medium-high about 2 minutes, until slightly syrupy, then lower to medium-low.

Whisk the cornstarch with 2-4 Tbsp of the hot syrup into a smooth slurry, whisk it back into the pot and heat until thick. Off the heat, stir in the sambal and the raw garlic (never boil the garlic). Cool to room temperature; keeps about 2 weeks refrigerated.

Filling: roughly cut the carrot, celery, green onions and onion and pulse them with the garlic in a food processor until very finely chopped but not puréed or watery. (This file counts about 1/4 of the full batch; scale down or use the rest for original lumpia.)
Mix the vegetables into the ground pork with the soy sauce, kosher salt, MSG, black pepper and egg. Knead like a dough until fully emulsified and tacky.
Split each serrano lengthwise, keeping the stem on, and scrape out the pith and seeds with a spoon (leave more for more heat).

Fill each half generously with the pork filling, slightly mounded. Lay two filled halves end to end on a wrapper with the stems poking out at each end, join them with a little more filling, fold over and roll up tightly. Seal the end with egg wash.
Cut the long roll in half to make two lumpia. Repeat with the rest.
Fry at 350°F in batches for 3-5 minutes, until golden and crisp. Drain on a wire rack and let cool a little.
Serve stacked with the sweet chili sauce, Kewpie mayo and banana ketchup for dipping.
